name: James A. Himes

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: HOUSING FOR THE 21ST CENTURY ACT
statements.title: HOUSING FOR THE 21ST CENTURY ACT
sentences: Our colleagues at the State and municipal levels need to take a hard look at the regulations, at the land use policies, and at the zoning.
Mr. Speaker, I urge my colleagues at this point in time: Let's listen to the American people.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: EXTENSION OF AUTHORITIES OF TITLE VII OF THE FOREIGN INTELLIGENCE SURVEILLANCE ACT OF 1978
statements.title: EXTENSION OF AUTHORITIES OF TITLE VII OF THE FOREIGN INTELLIGENCE SURVEILLANCE ACT OF 1978

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: UKRAINE SUPPORT ACT
statements.title: UKRAINE SUPPORT ACT
sentences: Five days ago, I was in Ukraine, and I saw what so many of us have seen: truly remarkable courage, absolute commitment to fighting for their freedom, innovation like you would not believe, and, interestingly, something I had not seen before in my previous trips to Ukraine, which was the optimism and joy in the face of missiles and destruction that the Ukrainians are winning.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: DIRECTING THE PRESIDENT, PURSUANT TO SECTION 5(c) OF THE WAR POWERS RESOLUTION, TO REMOVE UNITED STATES ARMED FORCES FROM HOSTILITIES WITH IRAN
statements.title: DIRECTING THE PRESIDENT, PURSUANT TO SECTION 5(c) OF THE WAR POWERS RESOLUTION, TO REMOVE UNITED STATES ARMED FORCES FROM HOSTILITIES WITH IRAN
sentences: The War Powers Act requires that troops be withdrawn, absent the approval of Congress, after 60 days.

It doesn't, therefore, follow that you declare war and go to war and raise Americans' gas prices by $1.50 a gallon and spit in the face of the Constitution just because we all stipulate that the Iranian regime is evil.
We have had no explanation for this war, beyond the fact that we all understand that the regime in Iran is evil.

Iran, as awful and as dangerous as they were--which, again, isn't a license to go to war--was perhaps in the weakest position it had been in a generation due to the war of 9 months ago, so the notion of imminence is absurd.
The chairman can say it over and over and over again that we agree that the Iranian regime is evil.
Does the gentleman believe that the Iranian regime is the only regime on the planet that would like to attack the United States of America?

If I could point out to the chairman--and I respect his military service--if he were, in fact, in a foxhole facing a .50- caliber machine gun, at least for the last 100 years, he almost certainly would have been in that position pursuant to an Authorization for Use of Military Force by this body.
Mr. Speaker, I urge the support of this resolution.

Well, I think what we should do is pause our military activities while we exercise the constitutional and just the smart act of debating a war which has now affected every single-- Look, if this body chooses to maintain the military action, I will respect the body.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: FALLEN SERVICEMEMBERS RELIGIOUS HERITAGE RESTORATION ACT
statements.title: FALLEN SERVICEMEMBERS RELIGIOUS HERITAGE RESTORATION ACT
sentences: Section 702 is the single most important foreign intelligence collection authority we have, and every day it is used by apolitical professionals throughout the IC and apolitical professionals at the FBI to keep Americans safe here and abroad.

However, as I said, we now have a binary choice, and the reality is that 2 years ago, Congress, on a bipartisan basis, with the support of more than 70 percent of the Democratic Caucus, passed the Reforming Intelligence and Securing America Act.
On January 6, 5 years ago, I was in this Chamber when it was attacked by the shock troops sent here to stop the peaceful transfer of power.
I sat there for half an hour as police officers with guns drawn tried to defend our democracy, so I take a back seat to no one in my concern about the abuses of this administration.
It does not use artificial intelligence to analyze collected data.
In the law enforcement context, which is more familiar to most Americans than 702 is, a probable cause Fourth Amendment warrant is required.
Let's just imagine under my example that Bill Smith is suspected of selling fentanyl, and law enforcement goes in front of a judge and gets a warrant to wiretap Bill Smith.
Now, Bill Smith, as the police listen, is talking to his brother, Joe Smith, and Joe Smith says, I will help you sell that fentanyl.
The police don't need another warrant on Joe Smith.
Let us not say that this authority should be subject to a radically different standard than a typical law enforcement warrant would be.

This program is controversial for all the right reasons, and what we are doing here is what we have been doing for almost 20 years, which is finding the balance between an authority that keeps not just us but the world safe and protecting the civil liberties of Americans whose information is incidentally collected just as it is collected when there is a traditional police wiretap.
I rise in support of S. 1318, the Foreign Intelligence Accountability Act.

However, we are where we are, and I am going to support this legislation because in my decade on the House Intelligence Committee, I have seen countless, countless instances where the intelligence obtained through section 702 quite literally saved lives.

statements.title: DIRECTING THE PRESIDENT, PURSUANT TO SECTION 5(c) OF THE WAR POWERS RESOLUTION, TO REMOVE UNITED STATES ARMED FORCES FROM HOSTILITIES WITH IRAN
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I have been listening carefully to my Republican colleagues, and they will get no argument from me on the notion that we have been at war with Iran for decades.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: DIRECTING THE PRESIDENT PURSUANT TO SECTION 5(C) OF THE WAR POWERS RESOLUTION TO REMOVE UNITED STATES ARMED FORCES FROM UNAUTHORIZED HOSTILITIES IN THE ISLAMIC REPU

sentences: The arguments are that Iran is evil, that they hate the U.S., and that they mean us ill.
I can say with authority that, in the last 10 years, Iran's ability to create mayhem, while still very substantial, is at an ebb.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: REMOVAL OF THE USE OF UNITED STATES FORCES FOR HOSTILITIES WITHIN OR AGAINST VENEZUELA
statements.title: REMOVAL OF THE USE OF UNITED STATES FORCES FOR HOSTILITIES WITHIN OR AGAINST VENEZUELA
sentences: The chairman's summer stock theater and cringey antics notwithstanding, this has nothing to do with whether there are troops on the ground in Venezuela.

Mr. Speaker, I have watched my majority friends completely abandon their policy positions, brutally anti-immigration because of this President, obliterating free trade, completely leaving behind everything that the Republican Party used to stand for, praising Vladimir Putin, and attacking our NATO allies.
We will stipulate to your argument, pathetic as it is, Mr. Speaker.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: DIRECTING THE PRESIDENT, PURSUANT TO SECTION 5(c) OF THE WAR POWERS RESOLUTION, TO REMOVE UNITED STATES ARMED FORCES FROM HOSTILITIES WITH PRESIDENTIALLY DESIGNATED
statements.title: DIRECTING THE PRESIDENT, PURSUANT TO SECTION 5(c) OF THE WAR POWERS RESOLUTION, TO REMOVE UNITED STATES ARMED FORCES FROM HOSTILITIES WITH PRESIDENTIALLY DESIGNATED TERRORIST ORGANIZATIONS IN THE...
sentences: I will tell the chairman that I have opposed every Presidential attempt to use the American Armed Forces without congressional approval since I have been here.
They may be awful civilians, I will grant you that, but they are deliberately targeting civilians.
We will stand with you 100 percent about how horrible that is, but do you know what else is horrible?

Let's stop trying to scare the American people, and for the first time in a very long time, let's stand up with the dignity and decency that this topic deserves and debate how we are going to address this huge problem while preserving our privileges and prerogatives as Representatives of all the American people.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: DENOUNCING THE HORRORS OF SOCIALISM
statements.title: DENOUNCING THE HORRORS OF SOCIALISM
sentences: Congressman Norman, a guy who put a .38 Smith & Wesson on the table when he met with Moms Demand Action on Gun Safety and who called for martial law to stop the peaceful transfer of power to stop Joe Biden from becoming President, decided that Stacey Plaskett should no longer be on the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence.

Good idea number one: Get rid of tariffs, which are a tax on bananas, coffee, vegetables, pasta sauce, pasta, televisions, automobiles, and burgundy, a fine French claret for my Republican friends over there.
I am not going to frame this as a parliamentary inquiry, but I am very confused.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: ANTI-CBDC SURVEILLANCE STATE ACT
statements.title: ANTI-CBDC SURVEILLANCE STATE ACT
sentences: Nobody knows whether a CBDC is a good idea.
A couple of years ago, I wrote a white paper on CBDC, and I concluded that it is not clear.
It could also, by the way, be a trusted electronic currency for an unbanked population.
Two hundred years ago, the private sector, which my friends on the other side of the aisle hold up, had issued currency.

Companies and banks issued their own currency, and this country learned that this was a terrible idea and that, in fact, the central bank should issue currency, which is one of the reasons we are who we are today.
You might give the CBDC at least some benefit of the doubt instead of being ignorant about whether we want to know the truth.
Let's imagine that the European Union, which Mr. Barr wants to dissociate himself with, puts out a CBDC that picks up real usage.
The truth is that nobody on that side of the aisle or this side of the aisle knows either, but we are going to forbid any inquiry around this to figure out whether it is a good idea or a bad idea.
It can kill you and is produced by burning coal, which is dangerous, so we are not going to research electricity or atomic power or the automobile.
Again, I will acknowledge that we don't know if this is a good idea or a bad idea, and we ought to find out.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: DEFENDING MEDICAID FOR FAMILIES LIKE THE CURRANS
statements.title: DEFENDING MEDICAID FOR FAMILIES LIKE THE CURRANS
sentences: Mr. Speaker, in this Chamber, as early as today, we may be passing legislation that is explicitly designed to maintain historically low tax rates on the Nation's wealthiest people.

The problem is this comes with a cost, and that cost will be paid, as the Republicans have laid it out for us to see, by the Medicaid program and by the addition of trillions of dollars to the United States debt.
Let's talk for a second about Medicaid because it serves about 80 million Americans.
It exists, but it does not exist in any conceivable number that the Republicans are talking about cutting out of the Medicaid program.
As I said, Medicaid covers 80 million Americans with health insurance.
The real threat to Conner is what is going to happen in this Chamber this week as they find a way to slash Medicaid.
My colleagues are voting this week on what kind of future, if any, Conner can expect and what kind of future, if any, 80 million Americans who rely on Medicaid will have.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: FBI DESERVES OUR SUPPORT
statements.title: FBI DESERVES OUR SUPPORT
sentences: The Constitution of the United States says that birthright citizenship is a fundamental constitutional right, but that doesn't matter.
USAID is a legally established organization, whatever you may think of it.

What concerns me as the ranking member of the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, much of what I am seeing out there is the attack, the purge of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the FBI, which Americans know is the premier law enforcement agency on this planet.

We hear that the FBI is being told that anyone who worked on the January 6 prosecutions, when this building was attacked and 140 police officers were assaulted, that they must be on a list, undoubtedly for retribution.
I heard my colleague, Jim Jordan, just this weekend on Fox News once again promoting the conspiracy theory that the FBI was somehow involved in the attack on this Capitol on January 6.
Not one of them was authorized to break any law or to participate in January 6.
There were no undercover FBI agents here in the Capitol on January 6.

There will be an increase in violent crime, and I promise you, Mr. Speaker, I will stand right here to hold those accountable for the attack on this storied American institution and the carnage it will visit on the American people if this keeps up.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: General Leave
statements.title: General Leave
sentences: They broke windows, and they attacked police officers with heavy objects, with bear spray, with their fists, with anything at hand.
There were 140 police officers who were assaulted.
Let me say that again: There were 140 police officers who were assaulted that day.
We saw the Capitol Police with weapons drawn as an object broke the window of the main door to the House.
We watched the Capitol Police move a heavy article of furniture.
The new President pardoned every single person, including those involved in those assaults on 140 police officers--every single one of them.
Then, very shortly thereafter, he reconstituted a committee to investigate the people who investigated what happened here on January 6.
Oh gosh, maybe the people who assaulted 140 police officers were just, like, tourists.
Those of us who put up the signs on our office doors saying: Thank you, Capitol Police, only to turn around and remain silent when the attackers of the Capitol Police were pardoned on Monday.
Capitol Police Officer Brian Sicknick, he stood outside the gates here and fended off the attackers as they bear sprayed him in the face and eyes.
The very next day, Officer Sicknick suffered two strokes and ultimately died, making him the first fatality of January 6.
Officer Brian Sicknick was only the fourth Capitol Police officer to die in the line of duty.
Officer Jeffrey Smith of the Metropolitan Police Department, he fought off rioters in the Capitol that day only to be struck in the face by a metal pole as the siege continued that night.
On January 6, Officer Liebengood was posted to Senate security where he faced down the rioters.
He came back to work, despite what he had seen on January 6, on January 7, January 8, and January 9, unwilling to quit and inconvenience his fellow, similarly depleted and exhausted, officers.
Officer Gunther Hashida was a decorated Metropolitan Police Department officer.
He served on the Department's emergency response team and responded here on January 6.
He had been on the job for 5 years when he deployed to the riot, to the insurrection.
The first question I have is: We put up the signs on the doors that say: Thank you, brave police officers.
Yeah, I was bad on January 6, but what about Black Lives Matter throwing bricks through Starbucks' windows in Seattle?
This week, we learned that for most of my colleagues on the other side of the aisle, the pardon of the attackers of these police officers was not outside that line.
The plaque reads: ``On behalf of a grateful Congress, this plaque honors the extraordinary individuals who bravely protected and defended this symbol of democracy on January 6, 2021.
